title: Ottawa to purchase credits from carbon-removal startups to offset its emissions
html:
Deep Sky Corp. runs a project that's included in the program. Its direct air capture facility is located in Innisfail, Alta.Todd Korol/Reuters

Ottawa has established a program for federal departments to buy credits from 19 carbon-removal projects across the country under a plan to offset emissions from government operations.

The federal Liberals said on Thursday that the program aims to help achieve net zero by 2050 across government departments while supporting a range of technologies that extract carbon dioxide from the atmosphere and store it permanently underground or in rocks or concrete.

The projects, located in eight provinces, employ such methods as direct-air capture, biochar, biomass and mineralization to remove the CO2. The ventures span a wide breadth of sectors, including agriculture, forestry, mining and waste management.

Deep Sky Corp., Skyrenu Technologies Inc., Remova Carbon Systems Ltd., Carbon Lock Technologies Inc., Arca Climate Technologies Inc. and Karbonetiq Inc. are among the companies that have developed the projects.

Federal departments, agencies and Crown corporations can buy the credits under standing offers. Those responsible for operations in which emissions reductions are difficult, such as defence and security, are expected to benefit from the program, the government said.

Ottawa established the standing offers after a competitive procurement process. Two years ago, it committed to buying at least $10-million in carbon-removal credits to offset its operations by 2030.
summary: New program aims to help achieve net zero by 2050 while supporting Canadian technologies, the federal government says
